scope: Theorem 5.4 (Global sphere energies) of the manuscript “A Linear Clock for Random Walk on Tree-Weighted Planar Maps” (preprints/A-Linear-Clock-for-Random-Walk-on-Tree-Weighted-Planar-Maps-October-5-2026/linear-clock-random-walk-tree-weighted-planar-maps.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0acb1c84bf79e9c8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: From any subsequence of the tree-decorated sphere maps, one can take a further joint extraction and a coupling with the limiting ordinary quantum sphere such that the following statements hold almost surely. 1. If un converges uniformly to u ∈ C(S2), then lim inf n→∞ en(un) ≥ D(u). 2. For each u ∈ C(S2)∩W1,2(S2) there are uniformly convergent approximations un for which en(un) −→ D(u). Both assertions hold on the dual with e∗ n and π∗ n. 3. On every open set, graph-harmonic functions with bounded energy and bounded absolute value are locally equicontinuous under these locations and have locally uniformly convergent subsequences. This holds also on the dual and at the tour endpoint. All these conclusions may be required in the same extraction as the metric and measure comparison below.
